{{Top|canon=High Human}}
{{Citation}}
{{Quote|The Empire justified its actions through Human superiority&mdash;it was our duty to preserve order to prevent the exploitation of lesser species. Any action in the pursuit of that goal was justified.|[[Soontir Fel/Legends|Soontir Fel]]|<ref name="X-Wing Rogue Squadron 25">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 25|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 25]]</ref>}}
[[File:SatePestage-NEGTC.png|thumb|right|250px|Sate Pestage supported the ascent of High Human Culture.]]
'''High Human Culture''', also called '''Human High Culture''' or '''Human Supremacy''', was a [[Humanocentrism|culture]] that involved the [[Speciesism|superiority]] of [[Human/Legends|humans]] over other [[Species/Legends|species]] in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. It was enacted as '''High Imperial Culture''' by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] as part of its [[New Order/Legends|doctrine]].
 
==History==
{{Quote|It must be you [to assume the role of Supreme Chancellor, not I]. You have the political skills, and more to the point, you are a human. In this era only a human is capable of rising to the top of Coruscant's biased political heap.|[[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]] to [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]|<ref name="Darth Plagueis (novel)">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>}}
The Emperor's New Order was founded on the belief that diversity fostered instability, and its architects maintained that the Republic's collapse resulted from conflicting agendas that could only be resolved through a unified vision. This vision, they argued, should be shaped by Humanity, as Humans had founded the original Republic and ultimately ensured the galaxy's survival. Consequently, non-Humans were often viewed as incompatible with the New Order's objectives and were marginalized within the Empire's power structure.<ref name="Rebellion Era Sourcebook">''[[Rebellion Era Sourcebook]]''</ref>

There were several undertones that carried over into [[Anti-droid sentiment/Legends|anti-droid sentiment]] and anti-female [[Wikipedia:Chauvinism#Chauvinism as sexism|chauvinism]], which also manifested against Human females, who were almost universally barred from the higher echelons of power in the Empire's military and government. Exceptions included [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Natasi Daala|Daala]] of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] (promoted in secret by [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Tarkin]]), Admiral [[Betl Oxtroe]], Intelligence [[Director/Legends|Director]] [[Ysanne Isard]], [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Uwlla Iillor]] of the [[Corusca Rainbow|''Black Asp'']], and the highly decorated Pilot [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]].

Those not meeting the standards of Human High Culture were marked as being [[Non-huMan]].

At the time of the foundation of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], there were several active, minority populist groups on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] that advocated concepts of Human supremacy. These were quickly assimilated into the nascent [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order/Legends|COMPNOR]]. Their views were then coalesced into a coherent vision primarily by [[Crueya Vandron/Legends|Crueya Vandron]], [[Ishin-Il-Raz]], and [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]].

[[File:Confiscation-TCGBtS.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Non-Humans were treated as second-class citizens by the Empire]]
The chief tenet of Human High Culture was that Humans were the only truly intelligent and productive members of any society. They cited that it was almost exclusively Humans who had formed and led the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]] and the Human worlds of the Core were some of the oldest, richest, and most advanced in the galaxy.

As such, through the repealing of such laws as the [[Rights of Sentience]] and the creation of new acts, all nonhumans were made second-class citizens (if citizens at all). Non-Human slavery was re-legalized, and the Emperor's New Order cajoled the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] into repealing antislavery laws, passing legislation that discouraged or outright restricted aliens from leaving their native worlds, declared entire species property of the Empire, and imposed stiff tariffs on alien-owned businesses that attempted to engage in commerce with anyone but Imperial-controlled institutions. Within a few years, Humans and [[Near-Human]]s came to dominate nearly every aspect of interstellar trade and politics.<ref name="Rebellion Era Sourcebook" /> 

With the Empire persecuting many alien species, especially small groups settled on primarily Human worlds, many aliens flee to secret enclaves. These hidden communities sometimes operated [[Shadowport/Legends|shadowports]] to sustain themselves and maintain clandestine starship traffic.<ref>[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide|''The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide'']]</ref>

Only 'pure' (i.e., those made exclusively by Humans and with no help from nonhumans) works of art (such as operas, [[Holovid/Legends|holovids]], or books) were allowed to be produced, viewed, and spread, since only Human culture was worthy enough to be allowed to prosper in the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]]. Non-Humans were 'actively discouraged' to participate in government or join the Imperial military, and Human [[Governor/Legends|governors]] and [[Moff/Legends|moffs]] were placed in command of nonhuman worlds and sectors. There were loopholes, however: if non-Humans and Near-humans were devoted enough to [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], and focused solely upon serving his Empire, then they would be left unmolested. Examples of such tolerance were [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]], [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Bertroff Hissa]], and [[General/Legends|General]] [[Bentilais san Sk'ar]].

It could be argued that any roots for Palpatine's bigotry could be traced to the traditional animosity that dominated relations between the Humans of Naboo (Palpatine's home planet) and the Gungans who cohabited that world. However, It is debatable to what degree, if any, Palpatine was a speciesist.<ref name="Aliens in the Empire">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/96/indexp2.html|series=Aliens in the Empire|text=Part 1: Hierarchy of Power}}</ref> Palpatine freely consorted with nonhumans such as [[Mas Amedda/Legends|Mas Amedda]] and [[Sly Moore/Legends|Sly Moore]], as well as being an apprentice to [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]] (a [[Muun/Legends|Muun]]) and taking [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] (a [[Dathomirian/Legends|Dathomirian]] [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]]) as an apprentice, all of whom were [[Humanoid/Legends|Humanoid]]. Therefore, it might be suggested that as a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]], Palpatine's [[Humanocentrism]] was more liberal than that of the standard Imperial view, possibly due to the fact that Sith throughout history were predominantly either Human or Humanoid. Palpatine, or rather Darth Sidious, indicated in the ''[[Book of Sith]]'' that he did not personally adhere to Humanocentrism himself, but nonetheless viewed it as useful for ensuring a tighter grip on the Empire.<ref name="BoS:SftDS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref> From this viewpoint, it is conceivable that Palpatine's [[speciesism]] was broadened to include certain Humanoid species and that he used anti-alien sentiments as a way to divide the beings of the galaxy and help consolidate his rule. In fact, among the atrocities Palpatine committed was the destruction of the Human-dominated world of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] and the creation of a [[Emperor's Plague|pathogen]] that targeted Humans exclusively.

Even so, [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]], [[Lieutenant governor/Legends|lieutenant governor]] of [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]]<ref name="Cloak of Deception">''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref> who commanded the [[Outland Regions Security Force/Legends|Republic Outland Regions Security Force]],<ref name="Rogue Planet">''[[Rogue Planet]]''</ref> but also a covert servant to [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Plagueis]] and [[Palpatine/Legends|Sidious]],<ref name="Darth Plagueis (novel)" /> clearly enunciated a ''Humanocentric'' view that on first blush would appear to reflect the genuine galaxy-view of his [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] superiors. To [[Raith Sienar/Legends|Raith Sienar]], in [[29 BBY/Legends|29 BBY]], Tarkin announced that he performed "favors for certain people" for whom "balance is no longer necessary." These powerful, highly placed individuals held a preference or "appreciation for ''fingers''—not tentacles ... not palps, but ''human'' fingers—reaching into a great many stellar soup bowls, testing the temperature to see if they are ready for the eating ... Mark my words, Raith. ''Humans are the future''"; to which Sienar, himself a Human and a future servant of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] (designer of the [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|Imperial TIE Fighter]] and the originator of the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] concept), noting the tension in Tarkin's voice, responded, "So marked." Indeed, Sienar had sensed, as Tarkin now affirmed, that a shift in the "political psychology" of the galaxy was underway, that those beings who would soon "replace" the Republic's "effete elites" (beings who were rigid, inflexible, outdated) would "rule by brutality"; it was, in fact, "a law in the history of the galaxy. A kind of political balance, frightening but true." It was to this imminent perceived shift towards brutality in political rule that Sienar, only months before, had turned his "craft" of weapons and ship design (pursuing just such an angle of brutal, "centralized strength," though now he understood it was to take Human form) when he began work on his [[Expeditionary Battle Planetoid]], whose design presentation had left Tarkin "entranced." The Eriadu commander was quick to admit, however, that due to "the tolerance and weakness of our predecessors ... it could take decades to make humans the ''supreme race'' in this galaxy," requiring of them a ''magnanimity ''towards lesser races "for the time being."<ref name="Rogue Planet" />

Darth Sidious' apprentice, [[Count of Serenno/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] (Darth Tyranus), was apparently also a Human supremacist who desired to see the Republic transformed into an Empire of Man, with the Sith as its army.<ref name="sithnovel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> However, it is possible he developed Humanocentric opinions late in life from his association with Sidious, as in his youth he had alien friends and it is difficult to believe that any anti-alien sentiment on his part could have been hidden from the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] for seventy years. Many of his hand-picked Dark Acolytes were nonhuman, and he also seemed to personally respect [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosian]] [[Archduke/Legends|Archduke]] [[Poggle the Lesser/Legends|Poggle the Lesser]].

Human High Culture was enforced and imprinted upon the Empire's citizenry by the [[Coalition for Progress/Legends|Coalition for Progress]], [[Imperial Board of Culture]], and the [[Sub-Adult Group/Legends|Sub-Adult Groups]].

The views of Human High Culture would be kept alive in the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] for years after the Empire's defeat by fringe groups such as the [[Human League]]. At the same time, Admiral Daala strongly [[Anti-speciesism|weakened]] this concept within the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] by allowing aliens of all kinds to join the Imperial military. By the time of the [[Fel Empire|Fel]] and [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Sith Empire]], several aliens served within the Imperial military as [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]], officers and even [[Admiral/Legends|Admirals]]. However, by [[137 ABY]], individuals such as Admiral [[Dru Valan]] still believed in the innate superiority of Humans and resented serving under non-Human officers.
